extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers and editors evaluating Registered Reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers assessing Registered Reports in a two-stage process: Stage I (review of hypotheses and methods before data collection) and Stage II (review of completed study including results and interpretation). Emphasizes methodological rigour, pre-specification, replication detail, and editorial independence from result direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage I content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage I manuscripts should include only an introduction, methods (including proposed analyses), and pilot data (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage I focuses on pre-data collection elements; reviewers will be asked to assess the importance of the question, hypotheses, methodology and replication detail based on these sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of the research question(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance of the research question(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the proposed research addresses meaningful, relevant questions worthy of investigation under the Registered Reports format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logic, rationale, and plausibility of the proposed hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: The logic, rationale, and plausibility of the proposed hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether hypotheses are well-motivated by theory or prior evidence and whether they are internally coherent and plausible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness and feasibility of the methodology and analysis pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The soundness and feasibility of the methodology and analysis pipeline (including statistical power analysis where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the design and analysis plan are appropriate to test the hypotheses, are practically feasible, and include adequate considerations such as power/sample size calculations when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and sufficiency of methodological detail for exact replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the clarity and degree of methodological detail is sufficient to exactly replicate the proposed experimental procedures and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure procedural steps, materials, protocols, and analysis specifications are described in enough detail that an independent researcher could replicate the study and analyses precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specification of sufficient outcome-neutral tests (including controls and quality checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors have pre-specified sufficient outcome-neutral tests for ensuring that the results obtained are able to test the stated hypotheses, including positive controls and quality checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for pre-registered checks and controls that confirm the study can validly test hypotheses independent of outcome (e.g., manipulation checks, validation tests, data quality procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and handling of ethical issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether all ethical considerations of the study been considered and dealt with adequately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that ethical approvals, participant protections, data management, and any other ethical aspects have been addressed appropriately for the planned study.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-principle acceptance (IPA) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts that pass peer review will be issued an 'in principle acceptance (IPA)', indicating that the article will be published pending successful completion of the study according to the pre-registered methods and analytic procedures, as well as a defensible and evidence-based interpretation of the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that IPA is conditional: publication depends on adherence to the registered protocol and a defensible, evidence-based interpretation at Stage II rather than on specific result outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage II content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Following completion of the study, authors will complete the manuscript, including results and discussion sections. These stage II manuscripts will more closely resemble a regular article format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage II submissions add results and discussion to the approved Stage I content and are evaluated for fidelity to the registered plan and quality of interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of stage II introduction, rationale, and hypotheses with approved stage I
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction, rationale, and stated hypotheses presented in this manuscript align with the ones in the approved stage I article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify consistency between the original Stage I submission and the Stage II manuscript in framing, rationale, and stated hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to registered experimental procedures or justified deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors strictly adhere to the registered experimental procedures, or, if not, whether any deviations are reasonable and if they are still able to answer the originally posed research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether any deviations from the registered protocol are clearly reported, justified, and do not undermine the ability to address the original hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data adequacy to test proposed hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: The data provided can effectively test the authors' proposed hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the collected data, as presented, are appropriate in quality and quantity to evaluate the pre-registered hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' conclusions justified by the provided data
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors' conclusions are justified based on the provided data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether interpretations and inferences are supported by the evidence, avoiding overclaiming and ensuring appropriate caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification and methodological soundness of any unregistered post hoc analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Any unregistered post hoc analyses introduced by the authors are justified, methodologically sound, and add valuable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize any exploratory analyses introduced after registration for transparency (labeling as post hoc), appropriate methods, and real contribution to understanding; reviewers may suggest additional post hoc tests but authors are not obliged to perform them unless necessary to meet Stage II criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision criteria independent of results' novelty or conclusiveness; encouragement of negative results
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions will not be based on the perceived importance, novelty, or conclusiveness of the results. The Registered Reports format encourages the publication of negative results. Research conducted to a high standard should not be rejected on the basis of not containing positive results alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus evaluations on methodological quality and adherence to the registered plan rather than whether the findings are novel or positive; accept well-conducted studies even if results are null or negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer assignment and continuity between stages
rubrics_metrics.description: If the editor is not in a position to judge whether the registered protocol was followed as agreed, then the stage II manuscript will be sent to the reviewers who also reviewed stage I (where possible and reasonable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where feasible, involve the same reviewers across stages to assess fidelity to the approved protocol and to benefit from their prior familiarity with the Stage I plan.
